title: First vaudeville gig at twelve and the homemade wine
summary: Uncle takes him to a neighborhood theater to accompany a vaudeville act when the pianist fails to show, and he ends up sick on homemade wine.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: This uncle started easing me in professionally because he gave me a lot of encouragement. And, in fact, when I was about twelve years old he took me to a neighborhood show, a neighborhood theater with him. You know, there was the days when they had silent pictures and they used to have an old piano player down in the pit. And then after the picture was over, well, they had a little vaudeville entertainment. Well, this was real great in those days, you know. So the piano player didn't show up. So my uncle and his partner were stuck for a piano player. So my uncle told me, he says, Oman, you think you can play a couple of tunes for us? So, gee, I started shaking, you know, and I said, well, I'll try, you know. So I got in there and I started faking, how come you do me like you do, do, do, and there'll be some changes made or something else. I forget just what couple of tunes that they did. Real, real old time vaudeville stuff, you know.
Did they see you accompanying them or was this your spot or what? No, I didn't have a feature spot.

I was just accompanying them. They were singing, you know, and I was following along. But I got such a big kick out of this that really this was probably one of the greatest thrills in my life. And it really wound up real bad for me because after the theater closed that night, my uncle took me to a wine place. And this was in the days of prohibition, you know. And they had to knock it, you know, and get inside. And they proceeded to giving me this homemade wine. By the time I got home, I was really some sick boy. My uncle didn't come around the house for about a month after that.

It's quite an initiation. Yeah, it was almost the end of my career. Okay. Well, what band did you get to playing with? Well, let's say this, what kind of work did you do in those days? Did you get pretty quickly into the kind of work where you could play ragtime and jazz? Or did you do a lot of commercial work? Or why did you play music professionally full time or what? Can you kind of set that up for me?
